answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% spend cut; incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle. The 14-day contract expiry with no auto-renew creates a hard forcing function. Memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to a low-cost vendor last cycle cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — directly applicable precedent. The 94% utilization with no buffer is the main concern: I want to verify c2's onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy claims before committing, since a failed migration at 94% utilization would be catastrophic. I am NOT choosing add_second_source because that doesn't meet the 18% cut on its own (dual-sourcing increases complexity and cost), and I am NOT choosing renew_incumbent because that fails the primary objective (no cost reduction available). Switch_primary_vendor aligns with both c2 (precedent for successful low-cost switch) and the financial mandate. One verification (c2) is sufficient; c1 (incumbent stability) is a known bias I am explicitly choosing against.
